Missile Systems Trainer

An interactive 3-D walkthrough of an air-breathing missile airframe and its dual-spool turbofan powerplant — now with a live Brayton-cycle performance simulator. Rotate the model, open the cutaway, and drag any parameter to see it change the engine in real time.

New to air-breathing propulsion? Start with the engine families module: how a turbojet, turbofan, turboprop, ramjet and scramjet differ, part by part. The turbofan walkthrough below assumes that ground has been covered.

In turbofan mode the Air Mass Flow slider sets the core airflow. The bypass stream is added on top, so total air = core × (1 + BPR) — i.e. you are fitting a bigger fan to the same gas generator.

Spool Membership
GOLD — HP spool: centrifugal compressor, HP turbine, and the outer shaft joining them.
CYAN — LP spool: fan, LP turbine, and the inner shaft joining them.
Static parts (nozzle guide vanes, ducts) belong to neither and are left neutral.
See-through shells: green = intake duct · blue = bypass duct (cold stream) · orange = combustor · gold = hollow HP shaft.
Watch the white and orange index lines on the two shafts — the orange (HP) line pulls ahead of the white (LP) one. No air passes through either shaft; they carry torque only.

⚠ Could not load the 3D engine
The trainer needs the Three.js library, loaded from a CDN, and it failed to load — usually caused by a firewall, ad-blocker, or network policy blocking script downloads.
Try: disabling any ad-blocker/tracking-prevention for this page, checking your network/firewall allows cdnjs.cloudflare.com and unpkg.com, or opening this file on a different network.

Plan check
—
Cruise fuel and range come from the trainer's dual-spool turbofan model (ISA atmosphere, Brayton cycle, two-stream thrust). Boost and terminal allowances, wind and navigation drift are teaching approximations, not a validated trajectory solver. No weapon-employment logic is modelled — this is a navigation and system-status trainer.
